highlights.title: NASA dumped over 800GB of Artemis II data online
highlights.summary: If you thought you'd seen all there is to see from the Artemis II mission, you're wrong. This week NASA posted over 800GB worth of science data, images, and videos on the Artemis II: Sights & Sounds of Science site.
body: NASA’s treasure trove of images, audio, and video offers an unprecedented view inside a historic space mission.

One of the more exciting reveals was footage of the Artemis II team telling the ground team back in Houston about its observation of impact flashes. Impact flashes have been seen before, but these ones on the dark side of the Moon could have been the faintest observed with the human eye, and everyone’s excitement is palpable in the clip.

Alongside the dump, NASA also released a trio of documents that help supplement the trove of unfiltered data. That includes the Artemis II Preliminary Lunar Science Report, the Artemis II Lunar Science Operations Report, and the Artemis II Lunar Science Data User Guide.

highlights.title: Smith vows 'karma' will get Suljovic after antics at Swiss Darts Trophy
highlights.summary: Ross Smith has vowed that "karma" will catch up with opponent Mensur Suljovic after the Austrian encouraged the crowd to boo the Englishman during a last-leg decider in round three of the Swiss Darts Trophy.
body: The two players were deadlocked at 5-5 in their best-of-11-legs clash on Sunday afternoon, with Smith having two match darts at double 18 when Suljovic gestured to the crowd to increase the volume of boos, prompting the Englishman to miss the target and give his opponent a chance at the match.

Suljovic then nailed a double 10 with his last dart to secure the checkout and the victory, although his unsportsmanlike antics left a sour taste in Smith's mouth, later taking to X to post his thoughts after the defeat.
"I don't blame Mensur for me losing that game," Smith wrote. "I missed two match darts. Simple as that.
"Obviously it's impossible for me to know what he's doing behind my back when I'm throwing apart from the crowd's response.

highlights.title: Learning to use local AI is exciting, overwhelming, and frustrating
highlights.summary: I'm embarking on a journey I've so far been hesitant to go on: actually using AI on the regular. Giving my most personal data to cloud services has been a major hold up for me, but it's increasingly possible to run powerful models locally to see what they're capable of.
body: It’s like using cloud-based AI tools, but the privacy makes it more appealing.

So as part of my ongoing testing of the M5 Ultra Mac Studio, as well as experimenting on other Mac and Windows systems, I’ve installed some local LLMs and I’m beginning to tinker. Here’s how things are going.

I started by installing the open-source Hermes Agent on the Mac Studio. Hermes is a self-hosted AI agent desktop app that works on macOS, Windows, and Linux. It’s completely free to use if you stick to local LLMs. Since this M5 Ultra Mac Studio has 256GB of unified memory, I could run just about any model I want. This is how things quickly get overwhelming. There are more models out there than I can count, and some have specialized uses. Generally, models with many billions of parameters are able to do more than smaller ones with only a few billion. And since we don’t have to worry about paying for tokens when running a model locally, I figured I’d go big to start.

It wasn’t long to get up and running with Hermes and Qwen, and even make them controllable via my phone by using a Telegram bot. But then, I was presented with my usual nemesis when it comes to using AI: the text box.
points: I'm embarking on a journey I've so far been hesitant to go on: actually using AI on the regular.
Giving my most personal data to cloud services has been a major hold up for me, but it's increasingly possible to run powerful models locally to see what they're capable of.

highlights.title: To Reinvent a Stephen King Classic, Mike Flanagan Needed "One of the Best Actors I’ve Ever Met"
highlights.summary: But in Flanagan's latest, a modern reimagining of the Stephen King classic, Carrie, Sloyan rolls those various elements up into perhaps her greatest role yet: Margaret White (aka Carrie's mom).
body: Samantha Sloyan has played various roles across the Mike Flanagan horror universe, both empathetic and extremely hateable. Her scheming, self-righteous Bev Keane was the standout performance of Midnight Mass. In Midnight Club, she played a witchy herbalist with a dark secret. And she was a calming presence as Leigh Crain in his breakout Netflix hit, The Haunting of Hill House.

Sloyan's version of Margaret is far more complex and nuanced than the one depicted by Piper Laurie in Brian De Palma's 1976 film, or even the version in King's original novella. Flanagan tears the story of Carrie down to its studs and builds something new, with Margaret playing a more important role than ever before, though she's still a tragic figure, at best.
"I think she fails her daughter in a lot of ways," Sloyan tells Polygon. "She's loving her in the wrong way."

Polygon connected with Samantha Sloyan over Zoom to discuss playing Maragret White in Carrie, how she approaches playing complex villains, and what it's like being part of Mike Flanagan's troupe of recurring actors. Flanagan himself also weighed in to praise Sloyan.

highlights.title: Do we really ‘hold tension’ in our hips?
highlights.summary: The idea is popular in wellness circles, but experts say there’s no evidence that trauma uniquely affects the hips. Here’s what causes hip tightness and what can help. In yoga classes, on TikTok and throughout other wellness spaces, you’ve probably heard the saying: your hips hold tension.
body: Pain and muscle tension hit harder when you’re going through a difficult time. But should tight hips make you question your mental health? And what can you do to reduce hip tightness? Here’s what you need to know.
When you sense muscle tension in your body, it’s probably caused by one of two things.

The first possibility is not clearly related to stress and involves muscles resisting stretch even when they’re relaxed. Stiffness like this is a mechanical property that reflects how your tissues are built and used.
The other possibility is that your muscles and nerves are engaged in some low-level activity more often than they need to be; this does often happen when people are under psychological stress.

highlights.title: George A. Romero’s Season of the Witch is a slow-burn feminist occult drama
highlights.summary: George A. Romero is obviously best known as the father of the modern zombie movie. But between inventing the genre with Night of the Living Dead and his outbreak horror, The Crazies, Romero made two much lesser-known films: There's Always Vanilla, which I'll admit I've never seen, and Season of the…
body: After inventing the modern zombie, Romero made a feminist film about a suffering house wife turning to witchcraft.

Hungry Wives was supposed to be an exploitation film. The studio marketed it as a softcore porn, but it failed to find an audience — probably because the movie features minimal nudity, just one sex scene, and lots of talking. It was an undeniable flop upon its release in 1973. It was eventually rereleased as Season of the Witch after Romero’s Dawn of the Dead sparked renewed interest in his work.

While sadly, Romero’s original 130 minute cut of the film has been lost, parts of it have been recovered and restored, expanding the 89 minute original release to 104 minutes. An obvious reason for its failure, beyond the distributor butchering it it by cutting 40 minutes, is that, what Romero made wasn’t a softcore porn, instead it’s a slow-burn feminist drama where the occult is almost incidental.

Protaganist Joan Mitchell is trapped in an abussive marriage and unhappy with her role as submissive housewife. She eventually turns from therapy, to witchcraft in an attempt to escape her humdrum life.

highlights.title: Verstappen claims dominant first Singapore GP win
highlights.summary: Max Verstappen won the Singapore Grand Prix for the first time in his Formula 1 career with a dominant victory, while Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton endured a messy race strategically to tumble off the podium late on.
body: Verstappen led every lap on his way to a second consecutive win despite being unable to communicate with the team due to a radio problem, but it did not affect him as he held off an early challenge from Ferrari's Charles Leclerc who eventually finished seven seconds behind in second.

Kimi Antonelli took advantage of an elbows-out battle late on between Hamilton and McLaren's Lando Norris, with the seven-time world champion on old tyres in the latter stages, to take third and extend his lead over George Russell to 102 points in the Drivers' Championship.
It means Antonelli can become world champion at the next race in Austin on October 23-25, live on Sky Sports F1, should he outscore Russell by 23 points and Hamilton by 14 points.
Russell recovered to ninth in Sunday's race after starting 19th due to grid penalties for a new power unit, as overtaking proved very difficult at the Marina Bay Street Circuit.

highlights.title: What’s my first decision as CEO? I’m giving myself the day off | Polly Hudson
highlights.summary: A life coach has helpfully pointed out that we’re all chief executives of our own existence. So let’s start enjoying the perks. To-do lists are done, apparently: the latest tactic to motivate and galvanise yourself is a “CEO hour”.
body: Katzler is against the to-do list because she sees it as “our fast track to feeling like we’re completely out of control, because we can never get through it. When you never get that sense of achievement, what you’re left with is a feeling of failure.”

Instead she suggests asking yourself what your wins were from the last week, which tasks you’ve been avoiding, and how you’re managing your energy, time and workload. Also, noting any eureka moments you had, how well you took care of yourself, and what support you need.

Scoff all you like, but for me even the idea of a CEO hour was impactful, because I noticed that my immediate instincts were to wonder how low the bar was for what constituted a win of the week (does “lived to tell the tale” count?) and worry about a boardroom coup. My company felt much more unfortunate Apprentice candidate than Fortune 500.

We also got a new trailer for Godzilla Minus Zero, the sequel to director Takashi Yamazaki’s gloriously grounded kaiju epic, Godzilla Minus One, which became a major international hit and snagged an Oscar for best visual effects.

Godzilla Minus One focused on kamikaze pilot Kōichi Shikishima, who struggled with survivor’s guilt after he failed to take action when Godzilla attacked the Japanese base on Odo Island in 1945. Kōichi was one of only two survivors and rebuilt a life with a woman named Noriko and the orphaned baby she rescued, Akiko. But then Godzilla re-emerged, and Kōichi resolved to die fighting the monster to atone for Odo Island.

highlights.title: I Made Terrible Games With Google’s AI Playground
highlights.summary: A long day’s haul in the video game slop mines.
body: Neon Don is really pissed at his ex-wife’s lawyer. He’ll tell you any chance he gets while he shotguns lines of pixelated bad guys. He’s also not real—his likeness has only existed for a few minutes in a top-down cyberpunk-style shooter game, generated in the Google Labs service Playground.
“Keep shooting!” Neon Don says as he mows enemies down. “Brenda took everything else away!”

Playground, which Google launched this week, is part of Google Labs, the company’s landing page for its various AI experiments that haven’t made it into an app or official service quite yet. (Google has done this before with things like music production ). It works similarly to Horizon Create, the game generation service Meta announced in September.

Playground is essentially vibe coding for video games, letting people describe in plain language what kind of game they want to make in a chatbot-like interface. Playground then builds a working in-browser version of a game. You can add further instructions to tweak the design from there. If you have assets you want to use as a reference, you can upload photos, videos, or models. Otherwise, the visuals and designs are all AI-generated.

highlights.title: Palace stun Forest on Glasner's Selhurst Park return
highlights.summary: Crystal Palace turned Oliver Glasner's Selhurst Park return on its head, coming from behind to beat Nottingham Forest 3-1 after a remarkable afternoon in south London.
body: Glasner received warm applause before kick-off in recognition of the trophies he delivered at the club. But, as Palace took control, the mood changed, with chants of 'Glasner, what's the score?' and 'Sacked in the morning!' ringing around the stadium.

Palace owed much to Walter Benitez, who produced a string of superb saves to deny Liam Delap, Morgan Gibbs-White and, later, Chris Wood. His interventions kept the hosts in the contest as Forest dominated early on, before Daichi Kamada's first Premier League goal and Jefferson Lerma's first-half stoppage-time header turned the game around.

Yeremy Pino extended Palace's lead in the 59th minute, reacting quickest after Matz Sels saved Jorgen Strand Larsen's effort. It ended a run of 19 Premier League appearances without a goal for the Spaniard and capped a remarkable shift in momentum, with Palace looking increasingly dangerous after the break.

highlights.title: Halo Already Delivered the Perfect Master Chief Origin Story, 25 Years Ago
highlights.summary: Late last month, Xbox announced that development of the next game set in the Halo universe would be handed off to Activision. Then, earlier this week, a leak shared by Rebs Gaming indicated that Activision is considering a hard reboot that would double as Master Chief’s origin story.
body: Like many gamers in the early 2000s, I got an Xbox specifically so I could play Halo: Combat Evolved. I became so obsessed with it that I bought everything I could find with “Halo” on the cover, including Eric Nylund’s Halo: The Fall of Reach. I didn’t expect it to completely change how I looked at Master Chief, but it did, chronicling his experience as a child abducted into an experimental military program designed to create supersoldiers. The armored, weathered combat veteran from the game, like the rest of us, was once a kid. But even at only six years old, he was special.

The Fall of Reach begins decades before Combat Evolved, in the year 2517, when Dr. Catherine Halsey identifies John as one of 150 children genetically suited for the SPARTAN-II program. These children are abducted and replaced with short-lived flash clones designed to trick their parents into thinking each child is dead. He's then subjected to years of military training under Chief Petty Officer Franklin Mendez. All of this occurs on the planet Reach which, aside from Earth, is positioned as the next most-prominent human world.

highlights.title: 'Straight out of a loveless, passion-free factory from Protein Inc': the best (and worst) protein powders
highlights.summary: Whey protein powder is everywhere, but which ones will you savor and which will you choke down? The Guardian staff glugged them all so you don’t have to. The best (and worst) instant coffee, protein bar or chocolate bars.
body: Proteinmaxxing has gotten out of hand. It’s in everything from ice-cream to yogurt – yes, our protein has extra protein in it now. GLP-1 weight loss drugs are in part to blame; as Americans eat less overall, protein intake becomes more essential. And whey protein in particular has taken off.

The side effect: a price hike for whey protein concentrates as much as fivefold as demand sharply increased in the past few years, as we reported. In other words, whey protein powders are more expensive than ever.

So which ones are actually worth the steep price tag? To find out, we put 10 powders through rounds of testing. While many of our testers had less-than-thrilled reactions, comparing them to “watery coffee grounds” and calling them “Pepto Bismol-ish”, they weren’t all bad.

After a blind taste test in the Guardian’s New York office and a round of testing in our homes, a few stood out for their blend of convenience, nutritional content and least awful flavor – and one brand was unanimously crowned the winner.

highlights.title: Satya Nadella says we should assume all AI models are ‘compromised’
highlights.summary: In a lengthy post on X, Microsoft's CEO laid out his views on the dangers posed by highly advanced AI models and how to confront those risks. Nadella says we can no longer accept a world where AI is treated as a "set of nested black boxes" whose advice and actions we simply accept or reject.
body: We must assume a model is compromised and contain it from the start. Think of it like an emergency brake. An authorized person should always be able to pause or shut down a model mid-task. More advanced models will require more advanced containment technologies that we need to standardize on.

highlights.title: The kindness of strangers: In one of my darkest periods, a few compassionate words helped turn my life around
highlights.summary: I was standing at the traffic lights with the weight of the world on my shoulders when a man approached. He will probably never know the impact he had on my life. My cousin had recently died in a terrible accident and I had been the one who had to identify the body.
body: One morning during rush hour, I stood at the traffic lights waiting to cross on my way to the office. I was lost in my thoughts but must have looked like I had the weight of the world on my shoulders, because something unexpected happened.
A man walked up, put his arm around me and said, “Everything is going to be OK.” I burst into tears and by the time I’d pulled myself together he was gone, disappeared into the crowd.
There was nothing remarkable about him at all. In fact, I can’t even remember his face. But that brief moment shifted everything for me.
I had been dwelling in victimhood and this stranger snapped me out of it. His kindness gave me enough hope to make a change and turn my life around.

highlights.title: DistroKid has been quietly taking down songs in response to UMG lawsuit
highlights.summary: Artists are taking to social media to complain that DistroKid has unceremoniously removed their work without notice. Now DistroKid has confirmed to The Verge that the takedowns are a direct response to claims made by UMG.
body: Artists are frustrated with the lack of transparency around DistroKid removing their songs.

Musician and self-described “Video Game boy” McGwire reported that six of his songs had been removed from streaming. As has been the case with others, McGwire says that there was no communication from DistroKid before or after the removals, and that he had to contact the company for an explanation.

DistroKid also makes it exceedingly difficult to contact them. McGwire first had to have a “lengthy circular conversation” with a bot before getting hold of a live agent. One of the songs removed was a cover of Stevie Wonder’s “Isn’t She Lovely,” which he claims to have had a proper license for. Another track used a beat he purchased through a marketplace, which others had also licensed.
Most infuriating for McGwire was a song removed for an uncleared sample. The song he allegedly sampled was released two years after his track.

highlights.title: Donations to major parties and an ex-premier as a lobbyist: how datacentres play the political game in Australia
highlights.summary: As governments face community backlash for fast-tracking developments, big tech’s financial contributions face renewed scrutiny. Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast.
body: O n 14 June 2025, Anthony Albanese stood inside an enormous sphere of glass and steel, surrounded by 40,000 plants from around the world. His mind was firmly fixed on datacentres. The prime minister was in the Seattle headquarters of Amazon Web Services. He stood alongside the company’s chief executive, Matt Garman, who outlined a $20bn plan to build datacentres in Melbourne and Sydney.
Speaking to a travelling press pack, Garman was emphatic that Australia was “incredibly important and a great market” for the world’s biggest datacentre company.

Within days of Albanese returning home, Amazon reported its largest payment to an Australian political party on record. The company’s federal disclosures show a $46,500 payment to the Labor party’s federal branch on 28 June.
This was one of 34 payments – totalling $538,000 – that Amazon made to Labor and Liberal branches over a six-year period.

body: There are over 230 million copies of Grand Theft Auto 5 in the world. As the second-highest selling game of all time, it has been played for billions of hours by players across the globe, making it one of the most significant pastimes in the entire world. That’s an impressive achievement for what in 2013 was simply the highly-anticipated next entry in Rockstar’s beloved (and notorious) open-world crime series. But GTA 5 proved to be much, much more than a typical sequel. It has become home to a huge, expressive, and loyal community, one which has made a digital hobby of everything from warring alien clans to producing slick vehicle stunt movies.
This is the story of how a video game became much more than a crime simulator.

highlights.title: The Canned Vegetable That Transforms Creamy Pasta into a Comfort Meal
highlights.summary: I have seen a lot of canned vegetable upgrades lately. One person suggested adding canned mushrooms to a grilled cheese, and another said to pour canned collard greens over white rice.
body: Food Editor Patty Catalano recommends adding creamed corn to chicken pot pie, enchiladas, corn chowder, and chili to make the dishes creamier. Senior Recipe Editor Christine Gallary likes to add a can to egg drop soup. Senior Culinary Producer Rachel Perlmutter adds it to corn chowder to make it creamier without adding more dairy. But what I was really interested in was adding a can to Alfredo sauce. So I followed our recipe for the best-ever fettuccine Alfredo with a slight twist. Here’s how it turned out.

Who knew my favorite ingredient in a fettuccine Alfredo was one day going to be a can of creamed corn? Well, it is now. An Alfredo sauce is obviously already very creamy. The main ingredients, after all, are Parmesan cheese, Pecorino Romano, heavy cream, and butter. They melt together into cheesy, creamy perfection, which can sometimes be a bit heavy. Adding a can of creamed corn helps to cut some of that richness.
